en-US.author: Microsoft Corporation
en-US.description: A declarative language for describing and deploying Azure resources
en-US.longDescription:
Bicep is a Domain Specific Language (DSL) for deploying Azure resources declaratively. It aims to drastically simplify the authoring experience with a cleaner syntax, improved type safety, and better support for modularity and code re-use. Bicep is a transparent abstraction over ARM and ARM templates, which means anything that can be done in an ARM Template can be done in Bicep (outside of temporary known limitations). All resource types, apiVersions, and properties that are valid in an ARM template are equally valid in Bicep on day one (Note: even if Bicep warns that type information is not available for a resource, it can still be deployed).
Bicep code is transpiled to standard ARM Template JSON files, which effectively treats the ARM Template as an Intermediate Language (IL).
en-US.name: Bicep CLI
en-US.releaseNotes:
Features and bug fixes
CLI and module restore
- Add --config <path> to the Bicep CLI (#20412)
  - Use the specified configuration instead of bicepconfig.json discovery for every file loaded by the command, including the entrypoint, local modules, and using targets.
  bicep build main.bicep --config bicepconfig.prod.json
  - Support extends and merge the configuration over the built-in defaults. A missing file fails the command rather than falling back to discovery. See REP 0029.
  // bicepconfig.prod.json
  {
    "extends": "./bicepconfig.json",
    "analyzers": {
      "core": {
        "rules": {
          "no-unused-params": { "level": "error" }
        }
      }
    }
  }
- Retry previously failed modules on a forced restore (#20472)
  - "Restore Bicep Modules (Force)" and bicep restore --force now retry recently failed modules instead of continuing to report the earlier failure.
Linting and version constraints
- Add linter rules for cross-file bicep.version constraints (#20337)
  - no-conflicting-version-constraints (error by default): report when no single Bicep version satisfies the constraints across an entrypoint and its local modules.
  - no-incompatible-entrypoint-version (warning by default): report when the entrypoint's constraint allows a version that a referenced file rejects.
- Suppress redundant BCP104 diagnostics in VS Code when a referenced file's only error is a version constraint mismatch (BCP456) (#20388)
- Update deployment script Az PowerShell guidance (#20396)
  - Raise the linter's default minimum version to 15.0 and use version 16.2 in the deployment script snippet.
Visualizer
- Add support for matching the active VS Code color theme (#20395)
  - Enable with the new bicep.visualizer.matchColorTheme setting (off by default).
- Add collapsible modules and improve edge rendering (#20409, #20442, #20467)
  - Collapse a module into a single card and expand it again without editing the Bicep source. Both actions support undo.
  - Draw edges below the nodes they connect rather than over unrelated nodes.
- Add support for expanding registry modules published with source (#20471)
  - Restore registry modules on demand when expanded, and open their published source when a node is selected.
Compiler and decompilation
- Block @sealed() on resource-derived types accessed through expressions, aliases, and imports (#20389)
  - These previously compiled to templates that rejected every non-empty value at deployment time.
- Fix the WebAssembly decompilation API to return all generated files, not just the entrypoint (#20387)
Dependencies
- Update Azure Deployments packages to 1.812.0 (#20444)
Community contributions
- Add context menu option to generate snapshots for .bicepparam files (#19024) - Thanks @verschaevesiebe!
- On force restore continue recursing into local modules (#19137) - Thanks @martinjanocko!
- Fix misleading location warnings for invalid expressions (#20492) - Thanks @KevinDal2027!
- Update warnings for experimental features in documentation (#18605) - Thanks @aperezmicrosoft!

zh-CN.description: 用于描述和部署 Azure 资源的声明式语言
zh-CN.longDescription:
Bicep 是一种用于以声明方式部署 Azure 资源的领域特定语言 (DSL)。它旨在通过更简洁的语法、改进的类型安全性以及对模块化和代码重用的更好支持，大幅简化编写体验。Bicep 是对 ARM 和 ARM 模板的透明抽象，这意味着在 ARM 模板中可以完成的任何操作都可以在 Bicep 中完成（临时已知限制除外）。在 ARM 模板中有效的所有资源类型、apiVersions 和属性，从第一天起在 Bicep 中同样有效（注意：即使 Bicep 警告某个资源的类型信息不可用，它仍然可以部署）。
Bicep 代码会被转换为标准的 ARM 模板 JSON 文件，这实际上将 ARM 模板视为一种中间语言 (IL)。
